summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1936-1937). He served as Director General of Archæology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937-1968) and as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1968-1971).
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She pursued her studies under Michel Hulin and completed her doctoral work under T. R. V. Murti.

Amanda K. Goodman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960-1963) and under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder, as well as B. K. Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, S. Katsura, M. Fujimoto, and A. Urquhart.

Amara Ali is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. In 2026, she is attested as a Lecturer in Urdu at both the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Amaranatha Jha studied at Colonelganj Inter College and Muir Central College (BA ~1913-1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938-1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947-1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indologist affiliated with the University of Calcutta (attested 1936). He also served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series.

Amartya Sen studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge. He held posts at Jadavpur University, the University of Delhi, the London School of Economics, and Harvard University as Thomas W. Lamont University Professor and Professor of Economics and Philosophy.
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed her PhD in 2009 at the University of Hyderabad, where she has served as a professor (attested 2018-2026).

Amber D. Carpenter is a philosopher of Buddhist studies who studied under M. M. McCabe, V. Harte, R. Gaita, J. Lear, S. Neiman, and J. Glover. Her posts include an Anniversary Lectureship at the University of York and associate professor at Yale-NUS College.

Amelia Bonea is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~2004-2007) and Heidelberg University (~2009-2013), and became a Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester around 2020.

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2012. In 2019, she held posts at Central Michigan University and as Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at Naropa University.

Amin Sweeney was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of London (~1967-1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970-1977) before serving as professor and South and Southeast Asian Studies department chair at UC Berkeley.
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. She served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, where her posts are attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1961-1978) and later as Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993-2003).

Amrith Krishna is a researcher in linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at IIT Kharagpur, the University of Cambridge, the IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024-2025).

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She has worked with the CNRS and held teaching posts at INALCO (2014-2016) and the University of Bern (2017-2018).

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University and served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014).
